belief: People like me will never be treated fairly.
origins: For many, unfair treatment is not a theory: it is experience, from jokes, suspicion, being passed over, or worse. Family stories of injustice add weight. After enough hurts, “never” can feel like realism. This belief deserves to be handled with respect, because injustice is real.
teaches: Scripture does not minimize injustice. God says, “Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor.” The psalmist writes, “You have heard, O LORD, the desire of the humble… You will incline Your ear, to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed.” Hagar, a mistreated outsider, called God “the God who sees me.” Amos cries, “Let justice roll on like a river.” God sees, hears, and will judge justly, and He calls His people to act. The word “never” goes beyond what is true: God’s justice is coming, and good people in every community work for it.
self_statements: The system is rigged against people like me.
No matter what I do, I will be judged first by my background.
There is no point in trying.
They will never see us as equal.
errors: Predicting that unfairness will always win.
Assuming everyone will treat me unfairly.
Imagining no good outcomes at all.
Feeling hurt and concluding that hope is foolish.
questions: What real experiences of unfairness have I had, and how have they affected me?
Where have I also been treated with respect or fairness?
What does God say about justice and the oppressed?
What can I do, even in small ways, to seek justice or support others?
Who around me offers solidarity or understanding?
How can I stay hopeful without denying the pain?
truth: Injustice is real, and God sees it. He hears the humble and promises justice. I can grieve, speak up where I can, and work with others for fairness, without letting “never” take away my hope.
hw_truths: Injustice is real and not the last word.
log: Each week, note one way you were treated fairly and one way you spoke up or supported someone.
actions: Write the experiences honestly with a trusted friend or counselor.
Support a cause, speak up kindly, or mentor someone.
Bring your grief and your hope to God.
prayer: God who sees, You know every unfair word and act. Hear the cry of the humble, bring justice, and give me courage and hope. Use me to bring Your fairness where I can. Amen.
hw_questions: What unfair experiences have I had?
What does God say about justice?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God sees me and hears the humble.”
